## Où j'en suis
`analytics-staging` has been on PostgreSQL 17.2 since 14:20 UTC on Nov 17 (blue/green, 41 s of refused writes), pg_partman is at 5.1.0 with maintenance green on `events_raw`/`events_daily`, and the post-upgrade dbt run passed (14 models, +3% runtime, within noise). PR #57 is still open as a draft; prod stays behind `pg17_enabled = false`, and the runbook now carries the logical-replication + reboot step prod will need. Prod is held until Maya signs off after a full week on staging (s3-06, s3-08, s3-10, src-pr57, src-slack-infra)

- [en-cours] A full week of staging on 17.2 without incident, as the condition for prod sign-off (s3-09, src-linear-kes298)
- [prochaine-étape] Get Maya's sign-off, then pick the prod window outside the 01:00–03:30 UTC dbt lock (s3-09, s1-05, s1-04)
- [prochaine-étape] On prod: step 0 is set `rds.logical_replication = 1` and reboot, before creating the blue/green deployment (s3-10, s3-06)
- [essai-raté] `terraform init -upgrade` pulled AWS provider v6 and produced 37 unrelated changes in the plan; abandoned (s1-01, s1-02)
- [essai-raté] Applying the staging plan failed — blue/green needs `rds.logical_replication = 1` on the source parameter group; fixed by adding it and rebooting (s3-04, s3-06)
- [question] Which production window to take once sign-off arrives (s3-10, s1-05)
- [décision] AWS provider pinned to 5.82, no v6 in this PR (s1-02)
- [décision] `apply_immediately` stays false and no prod date until Maya signs off (s1-04)
